CHN.note: World's #1 groundnut producer ~19 Mt in-shell (USDA PSD MY2024/25, ~37% of global). Most is crushed for oil or eaten domestically. China-reported HS1202 imports 2024 ~760 kt (UN Comtrade): Sudan 352, Senegal 306, USA 93 confirmed exact vs FAOSTAT seed. China also exports ~0.5 Mt of shelled/processing peanuts to SE Asia and the EU.

IND.note: #2 producer ~7.1 Mt in-shell (USDA PSD MY2024/25). Major exporter of edible/HPS groundnut kernels to SE Asia: India-reported and partner-reported HS1202 flows 2024 include IND->IDN 277 (confirmed exact vs UN Comtrade Indonesia-report), IND->PHL 56, IND->MYS 47, IND->THA 43. Monsoon-dependent kharif crop drives year-to-year swing.

NGA.note: #3 producer ~4.3 Mt in-shell (USDA PSD MY2024/25) but almost entirely consumed/crushed domestically; negligible formal HS1202 exports. Smallholder-dominated; aflatoxin contamination and lack of EU-compliant grading keep Nigeria out of the export-grade trade despite its scale (2024).

USA.note: #4 producer ~2.95 Mt in-shell (USDA PSD MY2024/25, third-largest US crop on record). #1 supplier to North America and a major shelled-peanut exporter. FAOSTAT/Comtrade 2024 partner-reports: USA->MEX 161, USA->CAN 107, USA->CHN 93 (confirmed exact vs China-report), USA->NLD 70, USA->GBR 23. Runner/Virginia/Spanish types.

ARG.note: ~1.8 Mt in-shell (USDA PSD MY2024/25) and the world's #1 exporter of confectionery/blanched HPS peanut kernels to the EU. Cordoba-province cluster ships almost the entire crop. FAOSTAT 2024 partner-reports: ARG->NLD 202 (the largest single ARG leg, EU entrepot), ARG->GBR 45, ARG->POL 36, ARG->FRA 20, ARG->ESP 20, ARG->ITA 19, ARG->DEU 18, ARG->AUS 16.

SEN.note: ~0.8 Mt 2024/25, on track to overtake Sudan as Africa's #2 producer (USDA/Ecofin 2025). China buys most of Senegal's exportable in-shell crop: China-reported HS1202 import from Senegal 306 kt in 2024 (UN Comtrade, confirmed exact vs FAOSTAT seed) — a politically sensitive flow as it diverts nuts from domestic crushing (Sonacos).

SDN.note: ~1.0 Mt 2024/25 despite the civil war disrupting Kordofan/Gezira output (USDA/IndexBox 2025). Sudan is the single largest groundnut supplier to China: China-reported HS1202 import from Sudan 352 kt in 2024 (UN Comtrade, confirmed exact vs FAOSTAT seed) — the world's #1 bilateral groundnut flow.

BRA.note: Fast-growing Sao Paulo peanut cluster ~0.9 Mt 2024/25 (USDA PSD), an increasingly important HPS/blanched-kernel exporter rivalling Argentina on quality. FAOSTAT 2024 partner-reports: BRA->ZAF 31, BRA->NLD 23. Largely planted in rotation with sugarcane.

NLD.note: Europe's primary groundnut entrepot (Rotterdam): imports Argentine/Brazilian/US/Chinese kernels, re-exports onward across the EU. FAOSTAT 2024 partner-reports into NLD include ARG 202, USA 70, CHN 25, BRA 23, NIC 17; NLD then re-exports e.g. NLD->DEU 70, NLD->POL 21 (2024).

IDN.note: Large net importer for its snack/tempe/peanut-sauce demand. Indonesia-reported HS1202 imports 2024 ~360 kt (UN Comtrade): India 277 (confirmed exact vs FAOSTAT seed), China 49, plus Argentina/Vietnam. Domestic crop ~0.48 Mt cannot cover consumption (2024).

VNM.note: Both a grower and a regional re-processor/trader of groundnuts for snacking and oil. Imports Indian/Chinese/Cambodian kernels and re-exports some shelled product. Did not report a clean HS1202 series to Comtrade 2024; balance modeled from FAOSTAT supply-utilization (2024).

MEX.note: Major net importer for confectionery and peanut-butter demand, supplied overwhelmingly by the US. FAOSTAT/Comtrade 2024: USA->MEX 161 kt is the single largest US groundnut export leg; Mexico's own crop is small (2024).

ZAF.note: Variable domestic crop (drought-exposed) makes South Africa a swing net importer of edible groundnuts for its peanut-butter and snack industry. FAOSTAT 2024 partner-report BRA->ZAF 31 kt; also sources from Argentina and regional Southern-African producers (2024).

TZA.note: Sizeable East-African producer and a regional exporter. FAOSTAT 2024 partner-reports: TZA->UGA 33, TZA->IDN 16. Smallholder crop with aflatoxin and grading constraints limiting access to premium export markets (2024).

GBR.note: Pure net importer (no domestic crop) of edible groundnuts and peanut butter for retail/snacking. FAOSTAT 2024 partner-reports into GBR: ARG 45 (confectionery kernels), USA 23, CHN 18, NIC 17 (2024).

rankings.note: Groundnut (HS1202, in-shell + shelled) trade volumes in kt, 2024, blending USDA FAS PSD export estimates with FAOSTAT TCL and UN Comtrade 2024 importer-reports. Distinct from groundnut oil (HS1508) and oilcake (HS2305) and from tree nuts. Argentina leads exports of confectionery/blanched kernels to the EU; India/China/USA/Brazil are the other big exporters; Sudan and Senegal ship mostly to China for crush. Importers led by Indonesia, the Netherlands (EU re-export hub) and Mexico. China is the #1 producer but a net importer because most of its huge crop is crushed for oil or eaten at home.

companies.name: Olam Agri (edible nuts / peanuts)
companies.note: One of the largest global peanut traders/processors, originating, blanching and shipping confectionery and oil-stock groundnuts across the Americas, India and Africa (Olam Agri, 2024). Supplies multinational snack and confectionery manufacturers worldwide.
companies.improve: Should publish farm-gate traceability and aflatoxin-control coverage for its African and Indian smallholder origination, where contamination and grading gaps keep growers locked out of premium markets (2024).

companies.name: Golden Peanut and Tree Nuts (ADM)
companies.note: ADM's peanut arm — one of the largest US shellers/processors of runner and Virginia peanuts, supplying kernels, peanut butter stock, oil and flour to global food manufacturers (ADM, 2024). Operates shelling/processing in the US South plus South American origination.
companies.improve: Should disclose Scope-3 emissions and water intensity of its US shelling/processing and the share of contract acreage under regenerative or reduced-input practices (2024).

companies.name: Birdsong Peanuts
companies.note: One of the largest independent US peanut shellers, buying and shelling farmer-stock peanuts across Georgia, Alabama, Virginia/Carolina and Texas/Oklahoma for the domestic and export trade (Birdsong, 2024).
companies.improve: Should report grower-level sustainability metrics and the energy footprint of its shelling plants given its scale in the US South (2024).

companies.name: Grupo Olega
companies.note: A leading Cordoba-province Argentine peanut processor-exporter of blanched and confectionery HPS kernels to the EU and beyond — part of the cluster that makes Argentina the #1 EU peanut supplier (2024).
companies.improve: Should publish water-use and agrochemical-stewardship data for Cordoba peanut acreage and traceability back to contracted growers (2024).

companies.name: Grupo Lorenzati, Ruetsch (Argentine peanut cluster)
companies.note: Major Argentine grower-processor-exporter of confectionery and blanched peanuts from the Cordoba cluster, shipping HPS kernels to European confectionery and snack buyers (2024).
companies.improve: Should disclose soil-health and rotation practices (peanut-on-peanut disease pressure) and audited residue compliance for EU-bound kernels (2024).

companies.name: Rural / regional West-African groundnut traders
companies.note: The West/East-African origination layer (e.g. Senegal's Sonacos and licensed Chinese-linked buyers) channels smallholder in-shell groundnuts toward China and domestic crushers — the engine behind SDN->CHN 352 and SEN->CHN 306 in 2024. Origination is fragmented and smallholder-based; firm-level export shares are not publicly disaggregated (2024).
companies.improve: Should build aflatoxin testing, traceability and farm-gate price transparency into smallholder origination so African growers capture more value than raw in-shell exports to crush markets allow (2024).

global.note: World groundnut (peanut, in-shell-equivalent) totals, kt, from USDA FAS PSD: world production ~51.4 Mt in MY2024/25. By country: China ~37%, India ~14%, Nigeria ~8%, USA ~6%, Sudan/Argentina/Senegal/Brazil/Tanzania next. ~55-60% of the crop is crushed for oil, the rest eaten as food/seed; only ~9% of output enters cross-border HS1202 trade. Export figure is HS1202 nut trade, excluding groundnut oil (HS1508) and cake (HS2305).

forecast.method: OECD-FAO/USDA envelope; 2030=2024*(1+rate)^6. Groundnut output grows ~1.5-2%/yr on African (Senegal, Sudan recovery, Nigeria) and South-American (Argentina, Brazil) area expansion plus yield gains; HS1202 nut trade grows faster ~2.5%/yr on Asian snack demand and EU confectionery sourcing, tempered by aflatoxin/quality barriers limiting African export-grade supply.
